newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 25.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
On 25th anniversary of United Nations admitting Beijing and ousting Taipei, commentary says Taiwan is pawn and toy of hostile Western forces out to weaken and divide China.
China's propaganda tsar Ding Guangen stresses the need for the Chinese press to follow the Communist Party and sharpen their political awareness.
China shuts down 50,000 heavily polluting factories nationwide, meeting 71 percent of the target set by the State Council, or cabinet.
Jiang Zemin, state president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, inspects a military training equipment show and calls on the People's Liberation Army to work harder to modernise.

An official from the State Statistics Bureau says investment is growing at a moderate speed and forecasts annual investment to reach 3.34 trillion yuan in the year 2000, up from the 2.15 trillion yuan expected in 1996.
